content_of_post_to_comment: Something I noticed about resilient people: They don’t have fewer problems. They have faster reset times. Bad news hits at 9am. By 10am, they’re back to their priorities. They feel if, process it, and move. The speed of the reset matters more than the size of the setback.
comment: The reset time idea raises an interesting question: is resilience built by reducing emotional impact, or by shortening the gap between feeling disrupted and choosing a response? The latter seems more trainable.
